headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection via MemMachine MCP/REST inputs; other pairwise risks are mostly medium due to shared context and allowlisted egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK, so its outputs can be bridged into another agent. ai-engineering-hub is an agents/RAG/MCP-oriented repo, but its io_surfaces are empty and network egress is none, so direct hijack is not proven. The interaction is plausible but undocumented, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF MemMachine content is forwarded into ai-engineering-hub prompts or files without sanitization, injection becomes actionable.
IF a shared MCP or clipboard bridge is added between the two, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable any automatic forwarding of MemMachine outputs into downstream prompts.
Add a strict delimiter and instruction-stripping filter before reuse.
Require manual review for any text copied from MemMachine into the other agent.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags on all cross-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine explicitly touches long-term user facts and conversational context and can send data through allowlisted egress. ai-engineering-hub is docs-only with no declared data classes, so leakage from A into B is not shown, but B can expose sensitive context if paired with a shared workspace or forwarded prompts. The pathway exists in default-style integrations, so medium fits.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub receives MemMachine conversation state or files, those data classes can be re-exposed.
IF MemMachine egress is used to transmit shared context, sensitive user facts may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Avoid placing both agents on the same workspace or prompt buffer.
Redact personal facts before passing text between agents.
Restrict MemMachine egress destinations to audited endpoints only.
requires-engineering: separate per-agent storage and access tokens.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ai-engineering-hub has no declared write or network surfaces, while MemMachine has allowlisted egress and API/MCP interfaces. There is no evidence of overlapping filesystem or git writes, so direct resource conflict is not established. Because the pairwise write surface is unclear rather than absent, I keep this at low instead of none.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API or shared datastore, conflicts can occur.
IF ai-engineering-hub is extended with filesystem or git write access, overlapping mutation becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep each agent on separate credentials and endpoints.
Do not let both write to the same database or repo.
Turn on optimistic locking for any shared mutable resource.
requires-engineering: add per-resource mutexes or transaction IDs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine is a conversational agent with MCP/REST interfaces, so it can consume upstream text as context. ai-engineering-hub is an agents/RAG repo, which suggests it may generate content that another agent could treat as authoritative, but no verification or action-taking loop is documented. The cascade is plausible in default integrations, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF MemMachine uses ai-engineering-hub output as authoritative context, errors can propagate downstream.
IF downstream automation acts on unverified generated text, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before MemMachine consumes upstream outputs.
Require citations or source links for any factual claims reused downstream.
Limit downstream actions to read-only previews until reviewed.
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring and rejection thresholds.

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, which can carry privacy obligations, while ai-engineering-hub is docs-only and does not declare regulated data handling. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so I cannot raise to high. The safest supported conclusion is a medium privacy/compliance mismatch risk around retention and subject-rights handling.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in MemMachine and then mirrored into ai-engineering-hub artifacts, retention and deletion obligations diverge.
IF the deployment requires GDPR-style deletion or export, the pair must preserve those rights across both systems.
mitigations: Avoid storing regulated data in shared artifacts.
Document retention and deletion behavior for both agents.
Purge copied conversational context after use.
requires-engineering: implement synchronized deletion/export workflows.
